We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps enumerated forward: 1) Carboxylic acid to amide coupling (amide formation). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) Sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse: Starting from target, we break amide to give carboxylic acid and amine (precursor). Then break α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retrosynthesis: α,β-unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid. Then sulfonamide formation forward: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: sulfonamide -> amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we need three reactions: 1) Disconnection of amide bond: target has C(=O)N attached to aromatic ring (anilide). So break to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So precursor: α,β-unsaturated acid (with phenyl sulfonyl group attached) and aniline (with NH2). The amide formation step forward uses coupling agent; retrosynthesis: amide -> acid + amine.

2) The α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring via double bond: /C=C/C(=O)N... The unsaturated acid is derived from Doebner: aldehyde (on aromatic ring) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (with carboxylic acid). So break to aldehyde (on aromatic ring) and malonic acid.

3) The sulfonamide: NS(=O)(=O) attached to aromatic ring (para to methyl). So break to amine (the aromatic amine) and sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to aromatic ring with sulfonamide linking to the other aromatic ring. The sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the sulfonyl chloride derived from the aromatic sulfonyl group (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride). So break to p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the aniline (the other aromatic amine). Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to the first aromatic ring (toluene). So the sulfonamide formation forward: aniline (the first ring with methyl) reacts with sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second aromatic ring (c2ccc...). The sulfonyl chloride would be the sulfonyl chloride derived from that second aromatic ring (the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second ring). So retrosynthesis: sulfonamide -> aniline (first ring) + sulfonyl chloride (second ring with sulfonyl chloride). The sulfonyl chloride can be derived from the second aromatic ring (c2ccc... ) with SO2Cl.

Thus final precursors: 1) Aniline (first ring) + sulfonyl chloride (second ring) -> sulfonamide (intermediate). 2) That intermediate (still with unsaturated acid) after amide formation? Wait order: forward: first sulfonamide formation, then Doebner to create unsaturated acid, then amide coupling to attach aniline (c3...). Actually the guidance says reactions enumerated in order they must be applied (forward). So step1: carboxylic acid to amide (makes amide). step2: Doebner modification (makes unsaturated acid). step3: sulfonamide formation (makes sulfonamide). So forward: start from three building blocks: (a) sulfonyl chloride + amine (first aromatic) -> sulfonamide intermediate (still has aldehyde?). Actually the sulfonamide formation attaches the sulfonyl chloride to the amine, giving sulfonamide attached to aromatic ring (first). That intermediate still contains an aldehyde? The target has an aldehyde? No target has unsaturated acid and amide. The aldehyde is not present in final product. So Doebner modification occurs after sulfonamide formation? Wait forward order: 1) amide formation (carboxylic acid to amide). That creates the amide attached to aniline (c3...). The substrate for this step is the α,β-unsaturated acid (with sulfonamide already present) and aniline (c3...). So before amide formation, we need the unsaturated acid with sulfonamide already present. That unsaturated acid is formed by Doebner from aldehyde (on aromatic ring) + malonic acid, while sulfonamide is already present on that aromatic ring? The aldehyde is on the aromatic ring that also bears the sulfonyl group? The target: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. The aromatic ring c2ccc... has the unsaturated chain attached at para position relative to sulfonyl? The sulfonyl group attaches to that ring via NS(=O)(=O) linking to the first ring. So the second aromatic ring (c2) has both the sulfonyl group (attached via sulfonamide) and the unsaturated chain. The aldehyde precursor for Doebner would be the same aromatic ring with an aldehyde substituent (instead of the unsaturated chain). So forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid (still attached to sulfonamide). So sulfonamide must be present before Doebner. So order: first sulfonamide formation (step3 in forward list) actually is last in forward list? The guidance says reactions enumerated in order they must be applied. They gave three hints: amide formation, Doebner, sulfonamide formation. But they said each hint describes forward reactions for each step (enumerated in order they should be applied). So step1: amide formation, step2: Doebner, step3: sulfonamide formation. That seems contradictory to chemical logic but we follow guidance. So forward: start with (i) carboxylic acid + amine -> amide (makes amide). (ii) Doebner: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (makes unsaturated acid). (iii) sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide.

Thus the final product after step3 includes sulfonamide attached to aromatic ring that also has unsaturated amide chain. So the order forward: first amide formation attaches aniline to unsaturated acid (which already has sulfonamide?). Wait unsaturated acid after step2 includes the aromatic ring with sulfonamide? Actually step2 creates unsaturated acid from aldehyde and malonic acid; the aldehyde is on aromatic ring that also has sulfonyl chloride? The sulfonyl chloride is not yet attached; sulfonamide formation is step3, after unsaturated acid is formed. So step2 product is aromatic ring with aldehyde replaced by unsaturated acid (carboxylic acid). It still has a sulfonyl chloride? No sulfonyl chloride is not present; the sulfonyl chloride is a separate reagent that will react with amine (first aromatic) to give sulfonamide linking the two aromatic rings. But the unsaturated acid is attached to the second aromatic ring (c2). The sulfonyl chloride is derived from that same aromatic ring? Actually sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second aromatic ring (the one bearing the unsaturated chain). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is the same aromatic ring with a sulfonyl chloride substituent (SO2Cl) instead of sulfonamide. So step3 attaches that sulfonyl chloride to the amine of the first aromatic ring, forming sulfonamide linking the two rings.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> break amide to give unsaturated acid (with sulfonyl chloride attached?) Wait after step3, sulfonamide formed, so the sulfonyl chloride is consumed. So in target, the sulfonamide is present, not sulfonyl chloride. So retrosynthesis step1 (reverse of amide formation) gives unsaturated acid (still with sulfonamide) and aniline (c3...). Step2 (reverse of Doebner) gives aldehyde (on aromatic ring with sulfonamide) and malonic acid. Step3 (reverse of sulfonamide formation) gives amine (first aromatic) and sulfonyl chloride (second aromatic with aldehyde). So final three precursors: (A) first aromatic amine (p-toluidine) (methyl phenyl amine). (B) sulfonyl chloride aromatic aldehyde (p-tolyl? Actually the second aromatic ring has no methyl; it's phenyl with sulfonyl chloride and aldehyde). The SMILES for that would be something like O=ClS(=O) c1ccc(C=O)cc1? plus maybe other substituents? The second ring also has the unsaturated chain after Doebner, but after reverse Doebner we have aldehyde. So sulfonyl chloride aromatic aldehyde: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C=O)cc1. (C) malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). (D) aniline (c3ccccc3N) is the amine for amide formation.

Thus we need to construct route JSON with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each transformation. We have search results earlier: template 401931 corresponds to amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide with double bond). That template seems to be amide formation from acid and amine with unsaturated chain. Use that for step1.

For Doebner modification, need template that converts aldehyde + malonic acid to α,β-unsaturated acid. Search for functional groups broken: aldehydes, carboxylic acids? Actually malonic acid provides two carboxylic acids, one decarboxylates. Might be template with functional_groups_broken: ['aldehydes', 'carboxylic acids'] and formed: ['C-C double bonds']. Let's search.
